current_activity: 116th Panzer Division listed at the disposal of the Fifteenth Army, place "Normandie", in July 1944
notes: Event date: Lexikon der Wehrmacht, 116. Panzer-Division page, table: July 1944 "z. Vfg." (at disposal), 15. Armee, Army Group B, place "Normandie" (Lagekarte); the next row (August) has the II SS Panzer Corps and the Fifth Panzer Army; no day, so 15 July is the middle of the month and an approximate date. Event definition: a month-level list; the division was in the 15th Army area before it moved to the Normandy front; the day of the move is not read in these sources. Location: Normandy, a representative point of the Caen to Saint-Lô front area, with a precision of 50 km. Location approximate: the source names only the region; this is not a unit position. Location support: weak: one source family and a region only.

location_qualifier: north bank of the Sée; division headquarters not stated
current_activity: Schwerin relieved at 1600; Col. Walter Reinhard takes command of the 116th Panzer Division, which had not attacked
notes: Event date: Breakout and Pursuit ch. 24 p. 463: at 1600, 7 August, Hausser and Funck relieved Generalleutnant Gerhard Graf von Schwerin and replaced him with Funck's chief of staff, Col. Walter Reinhard; thirty minutes later the division jumped off and made no progress. Location: the division was to strike along the north bank of the Sée toward Chérencé (p. 462); Schwerin had been threatened by American attacks toward Gathemo and Chérencé. Location approximate: the division headquarters place is not stated; the point is Chérencé-le-Roussel, the attack objective on the north bank of the Sée.

current_activity: 116th Panzer Division and 2nd SS elements retake le Bourg-St.-Léonard from the U.S. 90th Division
notes: Event date: Breakout and Pursuit ch. 27 p. 529: at dawn of 17 August units of the 116th Panzer and 2d SS Panzer Divisions attacked with infantry, armor and artillery and drove 90th Division troops from le Bourg-St.-Léonard and its ridge, keeping the high ground; p. 530: that evening the 116th received orders to relieve the 2d SS troops there. Location: le Bourg-St.-Léonard, named in the source. Context: the village is on the southern shoulder of the gap held open by the 116th Panzer Division.

current_activity: 116th Panzer Division covering the corps rear in two groups at Argentan and near Bon-Ménil
notes: Event date: Breakout and Pursuit ch. 27 p. 548-549: on the evening of 19 August the division had deployed in two groups, one in the Argentan area, the other north of the Fôret de Gouffern near Bon-Ménil; on 20 August the Argentan group pulled back north of the forest under pressure from the 80th Division, which took Argentan that day; the division prepared a breakout at St. Lambert for the night. Location: Argentan is named for the larger group; the second group was near Bon-Ménil. Location approximate: the point is Argentan, precision 10 km; Bon-Ménil is not in the place list. Commander: Col. Gerhard Mueller (ch. 27 p. 549).
